title: Dante's Italian through the published Naibbe cipher, written to a fixed margin
method:
Plaintext: Dante, La Divina Commedia (pin it_dante, public domain, c. 1320), the first 120,000 letters after Naibbe's own clean_line (accents folded, j->i, k->c, w->uu, non-letters dropped). Cipher: the published naibbe_v2.py at commit 5145f52, 78-card deck, RESPACING=17, UNAMBIGUOUS=True, Python random seeded 0, encrypting the whole letter stream in one call; output taken after the published 3 per cent optional space removal, the 'respaced' variant the author publishes as Voynich-like. The cipher writes each plaintext letter, or letter pair, as a whole glyph group drawn from standalone/prefix/suffix tables, with six homophone tables; plaintext word boundaries are not kept and the remaining spaces fall between cipher tokens. Layout: the cipher emits one continuous token stream; a scribe writing to a margin breaks it into lines of at most 43 EVA characters without splitting a token. Line breaks are therefore the scribe's, not the cipher's, and no rule refers to any glyph, position, page or section; the text is written once, in book order, 5,225 lines and 33,278 tokens.

What it shows (practice split, advisory): 6 of 28 established facts reproduced - F-006, F-013, F-014, F-017, F-024, F-031. The 22 it misses are the facts that need the text to depend on its own recent output, its page, its section or its line position. Two measures carry it: cross-word edge-glyph dependence (F-002) is 0.032 on the enciphered text against 0.230 on the manuscript, and page reuse of long words (F-009/F-016) is 0.153 against 0.311. It reproduces the low conditional entropy (F-013) and the sparse-vocabulary statistics (F-014, F-024, F-031) that meaningless procedures also reproduce, and no more: all four edge-dependence facts (F-002, F-004, F-005, F-010, F-026), all five page/section/language-grouping facts (F-009, F-011, F-016, F-018, F-020), every positional glyph fact (F-001, F-003, F-008, F-019, F-023, F-027, F-029, F-030) and every near-copy fact (F-007, F-021, F-022, F-028) fail. The gap is the cipher's, not this run's: the author's own published reference ciphertext (figure_utils/gaskell_bowern_2022/data/naibbe_reference.txt, 20,920 tokens, 10-word lines) measures 0.008 on the same edge statistic against the manuscript's 0.199. F-006 passes through the margin rule alone: packing to a fixed width makes the token that crosses the margin start the next line, so line-initial words are longer although the cipher has no positional rule - a layout effect, not language. This is evidence against a letter-by-letter cipher with randomly drawn homophone tables as a complete account: it matches local symbol statistics but cannot make adjacent tokens depend on each other or on where they are written, so the manuscript's edge dependence, lexical clustering and positional glyphs must come from something this class does not contain.
